content:
maria: quick check — I'm trying to wire per-model feature flags. current setup is one ConfigMap per model, mounted as /etc/models/<model>/flags.yaml and the app reads at startup. Problem: updates require pod restart or a fragile file watch. any recommended patterns? cc @lee @sam

lee: do we need immediate propagation to all replicas? if not, rolling update via checksum annotation is simplest. if yes, either push via shared cache (redis) or use a tiny sidecar that watches the ConfigMap and notifies the process.

sam: fwiw we did checksum-annotation in another service. example: add to Deployment spec.template.metadata.annotations: `configmap.revision: <sha256>` so k8s rotates pods on change. also works with terraform by computing the hash in a local-exec or using the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt` trick.

maria: thanks — want to avoid another infra service (redis) if possible. can you paste a small example of the annotation + how to compute hash from terraform?

sam: sure. terraform (simplified):
```hcl
data "kubectl_file_documents" "model_flags" {
  file_path = "./flags/${var.model}.yaml"
}

locals {
  flags_raw = join("\n", data.kubectl_file_documents.model_flags[*].content)
  flags_hash = substr(base64sha256(local.flags_raw), 0, 12)
}

resource "kubernetes_deployment" "model" {
  metadata {
    name = "model-${var.model}"
    annotations = {
      "configmap.revision" = local.flags_hash
    }
  }
  # ... pod template etc
}
```

lee: alternative if you prefer not to embed file content in TF: compute hash server-side and set an annotation in your configmap apply pipeline. either way, k8s will create new ReplicaSet. downside: short downtime during rollout if capacity small.

anika: can we use `subPath` mounts to avoid full container restart when only one file changes? my understanding is mount updates still require pod restart to pick up new file contents unless your app watches the file. correct?

sam: correct — configMap mounts are backed by a volume that updates, but some runtimes/inits cache the file. mounting doesn't restart the process. file watch in app works but is more brittle. annotation+roll is reliable at cost of rolling restarts.

maria: another question: some flags are sensitive (per-tenant toggles). should we be using Secrets instead? we don't want them exposed in logs.

lee: if sensitivity is about secrecy, use Secret. if it's just toggles that are not secret, ConfigMap is fine. also Secrets mounted as files are base64 decoded on disk — still accessible to anyone with container access. consider API-level RBAC and KMS if high-regulatory.

maria: got it. for per-model overrides that are small (a few flags), would we prefer a single consolidated ConfigMap with keys `model:<name>` or individual ConfigMaps?

sam: consolidation reduces number of k8s objects and makes rollout scoped (one change touches one key). but if you ever need different owners per model, separate ConfigMaps map better to ownership and smaller change blast radius. tradeoff depends on number of models (if +100, avoid one giant CM).

anika: ops question — if we go with checksum annotation, can we wire a TF plan check so that changing a flag (in git) surfaces as a plan diff (not just kubectl apply)? otherwise people might forget to update deployment annotation.

sam: yes — in our infra pipeline we compute the same local hash and include it in the k8s manifest generation step. CI `terraform plan` will show the `annotations` change. you can also have a simple pre-apply lint that checks `kubectl diff` between generated manifest and cluster.

maria: perfect. action items for me: 1) prototype terraform hash approach + deployment annotation, 2) short doc on secret vs configmap for flags, 3) add a small sidecar example if team wants hot-reload option. i'll post PR when prototype ready.

lee: sounds good. ping me on the PR for a quick review.

infra-bot: NOTE: reminder — config conventions require a short doc for any new pattern that affects deployment behavior. See https://redwood.internal/runbook/config-patterns :eyes:

maria: will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

anika: if you want me to run a canary after the rollout, I can schedule traffic split with the router.

maria: thanks — might do a 10% canary for first roll. i'll include that in the PR.

sam: small nit — include a one-liner about fallback behavior if flag parsing fails (app should default safely).

maria: yes noted. closing this thread — will update when PR is up.
